SM21A-A1.free_elimination: None cheap. 10109 is the 4-year value 4875(1.44)^2 and could be struck by 'P(3) < P(4)', but recognising it as P(4) is itself the multiplication. Options are not printed numbers or closed combinations of each other; ordering 8424<8564<8852<10109 gives no tell.
SM21A-A1.note: One Desmos entry, 4875*1.44^(3/2), finishes it; the 1.2^3 insight is optional. Distractors (half-period linear add, 22%/yr compounding, rounding to 2 periods) are all real errors and all reproduce. Easy, not medium.

SM21A-A2.free_elimination: None cheap. -8 is f(0)/the printed constant, but nothing in the stem rules out a printed value. In vertex form g(2)=(1-h)^2-9 with h integer, which excludes 1, but getting there is the solve (g(1)=0 gives h^2=9 directly).
SM21A-A2.note: Decision point is rejecting h=-3 (gives 7). 1 (vertical-shift reading, h=9) and -8 (shift dropped) reproduce. Solid medium.

SM21A-A3.free_elimination: No distractor dies cheaply. Pattern tell, not a strike: 5,6,7 are consecutive and 9 is the isolated outlier, so 'pick the odd one out' lands on the key.
SM21A-A3.note: Brute force confirms 9. Traps (strict inequality, ignoring negatives, both) are real. The 5/6/7 run plus outlier 9 is an adjacency/outlier tell worth noting; could swap 5 for e.g. 8 (miscounting endpoints) to break it.

SM21A-B1.free_elimination: None cheap. All options exceed the starting revenue 10080, so no lower-bound strike. Divisibility by 24 would kill 11532 (=12*31^2), but only once the revenue is factored as 24(10+n)(42-n), which is most of the solve.
SM21A-B1.note: Vertex at n=16 is an integer, so no domain issue. 13824 (sign of zero) and 11532 ($1 per step) are plausible errors; the 15624 story (maximizing 2n(504-12n), then evaluating revenue) is contrived but the arithmetic reproduces.

SM21A-B2.free_elimination: None cheap. 1 is the sum of x and also the y at x=-2; recognising it needs the solve. mod 3 does not separate: 11, 17, 20 are all 2 mod 3.
SM21A-B2.note: Graph both in Desmos, read (3,16) and (-2,1), add: one routine step. The Vieta route is optional. Easy at best low-medium; not a hard-route item.

SM21A-B3.free_elimination: None cheap. a=9 is readable off the leading coefficients, but that strikes nothing since b and r are unknown. 14 is the value at x=1 (a wrong method that gives a printed-looking answer), and seeing that is not cheaper than dividing.
SM21A-B3.note: Long division gives 9x+7-10/(2x+3). Shortcut: x=-1 gives -12=-a+b+r, so a+b+r=-12+2a=6. All three distractor paths reproduce (x=1 substitution, synthetic division without the /2, reversed subtraction).

SM21A-B4.free_elimination: None cheap. Showing the sum is positive (product of u-roots 8>1) is Vieta, i.e. the solve. No printed-number or option-set closure tell.
SM21A-B4.note: u=2^x gives (2u-1)(u-16)=0, so x=-1 and 4. In Desmos you can graph it and read the zeros, so it borders on easy. 4 (dropping the factor 2) is the best trap; it also equals the lone positive root, so it catches two errors. 5 and -4 reproduce.

SM21A-B5.free_elimination: None cheap. All options are >= -25 = min f (and c=f(0) must satisfy that), so no bound strike. 'Greatest possible' tells you there are two cases, but which pair is real takes the solve.
SM21A-B5.note: Zeros are 10 apart, so the other zero is 13 or -7 and c = 39 or -21. -21 (the other case) is strong. 4 (greatest b) reproduces. The 24 story (zeros 5 apart) is a bit contrived but coherent.
